problem: Specialized SAVN models need heavy task-specific training and generalize poorly to unseen scenes and unheard sounds. Multi-LLM zero-shot frameworks such as RILA are complex and inefficient (low SPL), and plain VLMs or MLLMs fail at long-horizon embodied action.
motivation: Omni-Language Models (OLMs) natively process audio, vision and language, so a single model might serve as the whole agent brain for audio-visual navigation. Obstacles are that OLMs cannot localize sound sources, are unstable at predicting discrete actions, and have short planning horizons that lead to spinning in place.
key_idea: Use one frozen OLM in an iterative pipeline of audio-goal prediction, waypoint-based global reasoning and a geometric controller, plus a test-time latent-token optimization (LNR) that selects target-relevant history frames.
insight: Sound-source localization is the bottleneck: the Localization Expert conditioned on OLM-predicted category raises SR from 12.6 to 39.2, while OLM-only localization reaches just 10.7 and random 3.4. Letting the OLM choose among waypoints and compiling them with a controller works far better than direct low-level action prediction by VLMs (SR under 15% even with oracle inputs). LNR beats K-NN history selection by 1.4 SR and 1.5 m DTG, so target-guided latent optimization is more useful than similarity-based selection.
method: AudioGoal Perception: frozen OLM outputs category scores over 21 SAVi audio classes each step; scores are accumulated with thresholds τ=0.12, γ=0.5 to form a candidate target set.

Localization Expert: plug-in module following the SAVi localizer, taking log-compressed stacked binaural L/R spectrograms and the OLM category score vector, and predicting K candidate source positions in agent coordinates.

Global Reasoning: QA-style prompting with a semantic map (following OctoNav); the OLM picks among candidate waypoints/paths using the predicted audio object and historical RGB, instead of choosing among raw actions.

Geometric Controller: compiles the selected path into a turn-then-forward action sequence with quantized rotation and step size; goals are temporally smoothed (ω) across iterations and the OLM decides STOP.

Test-time LNR: appends L placeholder latent tokens and optimizes their embeddings by gradient ascent on log p(goal | frames, latents) through the frozen OLM; the mean-pooled query selects top-K frame embeddings by similarity for the next reasoning step.

Global Navigation Instruction setting: new benchmark of 164 closed-set and 172 open-set audio-classification samples plus 248 visual-navigation multiple-choice samples, evaluating OLMs with and without a map.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-Omni-7B (frozen, main); Baichuan-Omni-1.5-7B (variant); plus a plug-in Localization Expert following SAVi
setting.training_data: none (training-free for the OLM; localization expert used without additional task-specific training)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB 256x256 + binaural audio (2-channel 65x26 spectrograms) + semantic map for reasoning
setting.action_space: stop / move_forward / turn_left / turn_right, compiled from OLM-selected waypoints by a turn-then-forward controller
setting.privileged: semantic map used in global reasoning; no oracle in the main RAO-Nav results (oracle only for Pure VLM baselines)

numbers.eval_set_note: 1,000 test episodes, unheard sounds, 200 max steps, Matterport3D
numbers.extra: training-free; semantic map used for reasoning

numbers_note: Benchmark is SAVi/SoundSpaces semantic audio-visual navigation, which is not in the canonical list, so it is labeled SoundSpaces. Global Navigation Instruction accuracies (e.g. Qwen2.5-Omni-7B all avg. 42.67) are for a new task and are not included in numbers.
results: RAO-Nav with LNR on Qwen2.5-Omni-7B reaches 39.2 SR, higher than all supervised baselines (K-SAVEN 34.4) and zero-shot RILA (35.4). SPL (20.7), SNA and DTG still lag the supervised K-SAVEN (23.4 SPL, 6.6 DTG). Pure VLMs with oracle inputs reach at most 14.7 SR.
limitations: Sound-source localization depends on a supervised-style Localization Expert; failure cases come mainly from localization errors, and OLM-only localization is very weak.
Path efficiency is worse than supervised models (SPL, SNA, DTG), with redundant actions.
Evaluation is simulation-only on 1,000 episodes; open-set audio classification and cross-modal alignment remain weak in OLMs.
